contents.name: Global Lefschetz number L(f)=I(Delta,graph(f)) and the smooth Lefschetz theorem (pp. 119-120)
contents.support: The global number as the intersection number of graph and diagonal, with the fixed-point consequence if it is nonzero; the page defines the geometric index sum and proves the theorem separately.

contents.name: L(f) is a homotopy invariant (p. 120)
L(identity)=chi(X) and maps homotopic to the identity (p. 120)
Lefschetz fixed points: graph(df_x) meets the diagonal only at 0 (pp. 120-121)
Local Lefschetz number as the orientation number of (Delta,graph); sign det(df_x-I) (pp. 121-122)
contents.support: The determinant computation is reused with the factor order (graph,diagonal), which converts the source's det(df-I) into sign det(I-df) = the local fixed point index; the sign reconciliation is recorded in thm-index-of-a-nondegenerate-fixed-point.

contents.name: Every map is homotopic to a Lefschetz map (parametric transversality plus Sard) (p. 120)

contents.support: The qualitative source/sink picture is absorbed into the worked sphere rotation example, which uses the determinant formula rather than reproducing the classification.

contents.name: A family tangent to a vector field at time zero has local numbers equal to the indices of the field (pp. 135-136)
contents.support: The proposition is restated for small-time flow maps with the explicit sign (-1)^n, which the source's order (df-I versus I-df) hides.

contents.name: Derivation of Poincare-Hopf from the Lefschetz number via the normal-projection flow (pp. 136-137)
Euler characteristics of surfaces via Lefschetz maps and the classification of surfaces (pp. 124-125)
contents.reason: The genus computation uses the classification of compact surfaces, which is published on its own page and lies outside this pair's closure; this pair needs only the sphere and torus values, computed from cellular homology on the companion examples.

contents.name: Exercises on nonorientable Euler characteristics and self-intersection without global orientations (pp. 126-131)
contents.reason: These exercises belong to the published DT-11/DT-12 intersection-theory pages; this pair records the nonorientable case through orientation-twisted coefficients (the double-cover transfer is retained only for maps admitting a lift) rather than through local intersection theory without orientations.

alternatives.argument: The definition is available independently: GP Ch. 3 §5 p. 136 defines the same local number through the degree of a family tangent to a vector field at time zero, and the Stanford notes p. 54 define the index of an isolated fixed point as the corresponding sphere map; the item uses the shared Euclidean displacement model, matching the in-run DT-13 definition.

The sign formula is available independently: the Stanford notes p. 54 state sign(x)=sign det(I-df) and GP pp. 121-122 compute the same determinant (in the order df-I, which differs by (-1)^n); the item derives the value from the in-run DT-13 vector field theorem applied to the displacement field.

The trace definition is available independently: the Stanford notes p. 54 define L(f)=sum (-1)^k trace(f_{*,k}) and the published finite-CW definition def-lefschetz-number-of-a-finite-cw-self-map gives the same alternating trace sum; the item defines it on rational homology of the closed manifold with the in-run finiteness supplier.

The theorem is available independently: GP Ch. 3 §4 pp. 119-122 prove the orientable transverse case by the graph-diagonal intersection and the Stanford notes pp. 54-55 prove Theorem 155 by the diagonal splitting; the item adds the perturbation and the orientation-twisted diagonal reductions, the latter constructed from published local-coefficient and Thom items, so no flow or lifting hypothesis is carried.

The sphere computation is available independently: it is immediate from the definition of the degree through H_n and the rational homology of spheres, which the item records; the Stanford notes state the same trace computation for sphere self-maps.

The failure of the converse is available independently: the published item cex-zero-lefschetz-number-does-not-imply-no-fixed-points gives a fixed-point-free-converse failure, and the index formula plus the definition of L on the circle make the stronger nondegenerate canceling witness here an explicit computation needing no external source.
